newsitem.title: CUBA: Peru's Fujimori pays surprise visit to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori pays surprise visit to Cuba.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori arrived in Havana on Monday on a previously unannounced trip to Cuba that was thought to be aimed at discussing the hostage crisis in Lima.

Fujimori, who flew in from the Dominican Republic, was met at Havana's Jose Marti airport by President Fidel Castro. The Peruvian leader was believed to be seeking to discuss ways of resolving the 76-day-old crisis, in which some 20 Marxist rebels are holding 72 men hostage at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

Fujimori had been thought to be returning directly to Lima on Monday after a lightning trip to the Dominican Republic where he held a 3 1/2 hour meeting on Sunday with President Leonel Fernandez. Officials in Havana had not said in advance he would be coming.
News reports have said Cuba, Nicaragua or a country in Eastern Europe could be potential places of asylum for the rebels.
However, the Cuban government has consistently declined to make any comment on such speculation. Fujimori has said he has not spoken to Castro about asylum for the rebels.

While ruling out considering the main demand of the rebels -- release of 400 jailed comrades -- Fujimori has indicated he might make other concessions. He has always left the way open to asylum in another country for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary (MRTA) rebels, who seized their captives on Dec 17.
